packets.title: Security-only deploy lane: sec/v1-hold-1 = production's deployed ref plus SWEEP-P0's fix commits, proven on that ref and deployed through deploy.sh, exempt from the product hold
packets.scope: Owner-run, under the seclane ruling. main after step 0 carries #208 (794 files) and PR195's payroll ledger, safe-to-spend and journal UI, and SWEEP-P0 is based on 0c22ea76 inside #208, so deploying main would ship product changes. Instead: (1) the owner reads production's deployed SHA (deploy-drift) and posts it to #80; (2) once SWEEP-P0's review repair is cleared by ChatGPT REVIEW (an external gate, not a packet), the agent cuts sec/v1-hold-1 from that SHA and cherry-picks SWEEP-P0's fix commits with the test commits they need (9b7d9e8f, 76b9b4d3, 6f4935f1 and their tests; re-resolved at admission), resolving conflicts against the older base without bringing #208 or PR195 code along; a hunk that needs #208/PR195 code (for example PR195's expenses gate on the purchase-order routes) is adapted, or the gap is written in the runbook as not covered by the hold deploy; (3) runs the full server and web suites, tsc, the 46 manifests and proof:release0 on sec/v1-hold-1; (4) ChatGPT reviews the ref; (5) DEPLOY_RUNBOOK.md records the ref's SHA, its base SHA, the cherry-picked commits, the deploy.sh invocation and the post-deploy probes; the owner runs deploy.sh. No agent touches production. Later security fixes ride the same mechanism as sec/v1-hold-2, -3, each cut from the last deployed sec ref: W11-KEY-CHAT-SESSION-BIND (a cross-tenant leak live in production), W11-MEMORY-PROMOTE-SCOPE, W11-FLOW-PERCEPTION-SCOPE, W11-CHECKOUT-PAIR-SCOPE, W11-STORE-OWN-PAYMENT-KEYS, the SWP-CENSUS-* batches and any secret read SWP-READ-SCOPE-CENSUS stops the line for. Fallback, only with the owner's explicit written acceptance under seclane: deploy main after step 0 and record in the runbook that the deploy carries #208 and PR195. The runbook record is merged to main after #208 lands (#208 rewrites DEPLOY_RUNBOOK.md); the sec ref and the deploy itself do not wait for step 0. WAVE-1 NOTE: Runbook additions from wave 1: (a) memorycleanup ruling (recommended): right after the deploy, run the one-shot MemoryConsolidationService withdrawal once per business from the server image (no model calls, re-runnable; command in (a lost scratch file, wave1-v1-result.json; work from this text) W11-MEMORY-PROMOTE-SCOPE open_issues). (b) stockcheck ruling (recommended): run the W11-PLANTED-STOCK-CENSUS dry run before the deploy and list affected businesses, since cash/manual completions of tracked products whose pair a planted row holds are refused until repaired. (c) A store's own Stripe endpoint must point at POST /payments/stripe/webhook (the legacy /webhooks/stripe has no store-secret fallback).

If the owner chose the fallback instead, his written acceptance that the deploy carries #208 and PR195 is linked in the runbook.

packets.title: Gmail and Drive clients answer a provider outage as 503 provider_unavailable, not 400
packets.scope:
Unchanged from the sweep-fix plan: Gmail and Drive clients answer a provider outage as 503 provider_unavailable, not 400. Spec inlined from the wave-11b packet file (scoped at fb00af1c; fixture prefix v99x_): This packet was scoped at fb00af1c. Wave 11a (29 packets, owner rulings D-116..D-139) has landed since, on the base you build from: read the current code and `git log --oneline fb00af1c..HEAD -- <file>` for every file in your write set before you start. Where wave 11a already changed what the packet describes, build on it; where the packet premise no longer holds, report a CONTRADICTION deviation and do the smallest change that meets the packet intent. Owner ruling D-73 (provider outages answer 503 provider_unavailable) and D-134 (409 finality). DEFECT (R-5 part 1; W10-DISPATCH-STATUS review CR-W10DS-1). GmailService (apps/server/src/modules/commerce/gmail.service.ts) and GoogleDriveService (apps/server/src/modules/google-drive/google-drive.service.ts) answer every non-OK Google response with BadRequestException, an outage included. A genuine refusal and a provider failure therefore look the same to callers. In particular, KEY's plan queue cannot treat a tool's 400 as final (see W11-DISPATCH-REFUSAL-FINAL), because reconcile_sweep_statements (flow-orchestrator.service.ts:4074-4093 -> statement-source.service.ts sweepGmail and sweepDrive) and drive_create_folder/drive_create_document (flow-orchestrator.service.ts:6133-6140) would then stop retrying a Google outage. Example: Gmail search 503 becomes BadRequestException('Gmail search failed (503)'), gmail.service.ts:1219 (the DS-02 case).

SITES (line numbers at fb00af1c). gmail.service.ts: 563 refreshAccessToken 'Failed to refresh access token'; 1023 sendEmail 'Failed to send email'; 1055, 1065, 1084, 1114, 1124, 1189 'Gmail API error ${status}'; 1178 sendReply 'Failed to send reply'; 1219 'Gmail search failed'; 1246 'Gmail message fetch failed'; 1293 'Gmail attachment fetch failed'. google-drive.service.ts: 322 refresh 'Failed to refresh Google Drive connection. Please reconnect.'; 438 listFiles; 457 getFile; 477 rename; 501 move; 512 trash; 522 untrash; 532 delete; 565 share; 581 createDoc; 596 createSheet; 611 createFolder; 635 folder search; 710 upload; 772 and 836 save; 921 downloadBinary; 946, 958, 976 getFileContent; 1053 and 1093 save-back; 1183, 1213, 1241 Sheets. Every one is an `if (!res.ok)` with the status available.

FIX. New pure helper apps/server/src/core/connectors/provider-failure.ts: providerFailure(service: 'gmail' | 'drive' (an open union for later clients), status: number, bodyText: string | null, message: string): HttpException. It returns new ServiceUnavailableException({ code: 'provider_unavailable', service, message, upstreamStatus: status, error: 'Service Unavailable' }) when the upstream failure is transient: status >= 500, 408 or 429; a 403 whose Google JSON error has errors[].reason rateLimitExceeded or userRateLimitExceeded, or error.status RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a 409 whose error.status is ABORTED. packets.title: Web handling of bootstrap 403 OWNER_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED: forget the stale workspace id, name the refusal on the OAuth callback
packets.scope:
Unchanged from the sweep-fix plan: Web handling of bootstrap 403 OWNER_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED: forget the stale workspace id, name the refusal on the OAuth callback. Spec inlined from the wave-11b packet file (scoped at fb00af1c; fixture prefix x01m_): This packet was scoped at fb00af1c. Wave 11a (29 packets, owner rulings D-116..D-139) has landed since, on the base you build from: read the current code and `git log --oneline fb00af1c..HEAD -- <file>` for every file in your write set before you start. Where wave 11a already changed what the packet describes, build on it; where the packet premise no longer holds, report a CONTRADICTION deviation and do the smallest change that meets the packet intent. CONTEXT. W10-OWNER-MEMBERSHIP (owner ruling D-104; reviews SEC-W10OM-3 and OMV-2) made POST /identity/bootstrap refuse a caller who is recorded as Business.ownerId but holds no Membership on any live business. The answer is 403 {code:'OWNER_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED', message:'Your access to this workspace has to be restored by an administrator before you can sign in to it. Contact support.'} (apps/server/src/modules/identity/identity.service.ts:1636-1700). Under ruling R-7 the operator backfill is the repair path.

WEB TODAY.
- apps/web/src/app/auth/login/login-form.tsx:173-183 throws bootstrap.error, so the server's text is shown and nothing navigates. This is fine.
- apps/web/src/app/auth/callback/page.tsx:225-227 shows the text under a generic 'Authentication Error' heading with only 'Back to Sign In'. The account_email_conflict view (:234-280) has a Contact support mailto; this one does not.
- Signup cannot meet the refusal: a new account owns nothing.
- apps/web/src/lib/client.ts bootstrapIdentity (:3089-3108) maps only account_email_conflict to errorCode, so callers cannot tell this refusal apart (BootstrapIdentityResult :3040-3045).

THE REAL GAP: the app shell. apps/web/src/lib/workspace.ts resolveBusinessSelection (:408-433) calls bootstrapFirstBusiness (:378-395) when GET /identity/businesses answers []. When bootstrap answers no business, it returns null without forgetting the stored kf_business_id, its cookie or kf_business_cache.

REPRODUCTION. A recorded owner whose membership a co-owner removed still has that business id stored. They reload /app. use-app-layout.ts:283-291 resolves, GET /identity/businesses/:id is refused, and every screen keeps addressing a business BusinessGuard refuses ('Not a member of this business'), with no explanation.

FIX.
(1) client.ts bootstrapIdentity: also map code 'OWNER_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED' (flat or nested message) to errorCode 'owner_membership_required', and extend BootstrapIdentityErrorCode. Change nothing else in client.ts.
(2) workspace.ts bootstrapFirstBusiness: after the existing generation check, when bootstrap answered no business, forget only the stored business: remove BUSINESS_ID_KEY and BUSINESS_CACHE_KEY, clear the kf_business_id cookie (clearBusinessIdCookie) and set businessCache = null. Never touch the token, refresh token or user cache. Do NOT call clearStoredBusinessId: that is the sign-out wipe (:293-310) and removes kf_token. The membership list was authoritative and empty, so any stored id is not the caller's; resolveBusinessSelection already replaces a non-member id when the list is non-empty.
(3) auth/callback/page.tsx: add CallbackErrorKind 'owner_membership_required'. It renders a view titled 'Your workspace access needs restoring' with the server's message, a Contact support mailto (same address and style as the conflict view) and Back to Sign In.
(4) login-form.tsx: no logic change is required. Pin that the server's text is shown and no router.push happens. Optionally show the same support link when errorCode is 'owner_membership_required'.

MUST NOT CHANGE. The bootstrap-once and concurrency rules pinned in apps/web/src/lib/__tests__/workspace-business-selection.test.ts, account_email_conflict handling, and token storage (a SUPER_ADMIN must still reach /admin). No server change.

OUT OF SCOPE. An in-shell banner explaining the refusal, the operator backfill script, and F-16/F-17 (ownerId arms on the server). SWP-REMOVED-MEMBER-NOTICE builds on its forget path in workspace.ts. Sweep-fix plan detail (inlined): (wave-11b spec inlined in this packet.) SWP-REMOVED-MEMBER-NOTICE builds on its forget path in workspace.ts. The wave-11b prefix x01m_ is superseded: SWEEP-P0 has since registered v99c_/v99f_/v99i_/v99j_/v99k_/v99w_, and x01*_ heads fail the registry's NEW_PREFIX rule (k<NN><a-z>_ or v<NN><a-z>_). A suite this packet extends keeps that suite's own prefix; a new suite takes the prefix allocated above.

packets.title: A removed member is told they were removed instead of landing silently in an empty workspace
packets.scope: Unchanged from the sweep-fix plan: A removed member is told they were removed instead of landing silently in an empty workspace. After removal, lib/workspace.ts falls back to the member's own business and the /app layout re-selects it (brief toast, then an empty workspace with onboarding, which looks like data loss). On a 403 not-a-member for the stored business: forget it and show a persistent 'You no longer have access to <name>' notice with the remaining businesses; never start onboarding for that reason. Pre-flight (D-274 A3, 2026-11-25, on main 892bb0dd + W11-WEB-OWNER-MEMBERSHIP-REFUSAL @ 2c3ef7ab): two mechanisms, both outside the original write set. (1) workspace.ts resolveBusinessSelection: when the stored business is not in the authoritative membership list, it silently picks the first listed business (or, with an empty list, bootstraps; W11-WEB-OWNER-MEMBERSHIP-REFUSAL forgets the id there). The lost business's name is only in the business cache at that moment. (2) hooks/use-genome-gate.ts sends a member whose remaining business has not finished onboarding (journey J8: the staff member's own first-sign-in business) to /app/onboarding. Fix: workspace.ts records a removed-business notice {id, name from the cache when it is that business} when an authoritative list no longer holds the stored id, and announces it; the app shell (app/app/layout.tsx) shows a lasting, dismissible notice 'You no longer have access to <name>' with the businesses the member still has; while the notice is pending the Genome gate does not redirect to onboarding. packets.title: Routing does not reserve storefront lines whose stock the checkout already decremented (F-36)
packets.scope:
Unchanged from the sweep-fix plan: Routing does not reserve storefront lines whose stock the checkout already decremented (F-36). Spec inlined from the wave-11b packet file (scoped at fb00af1c; fixture prefix v99d_): This packet was scoped at fb00af1c. Wave 11a (29 packets, owner rulings D-116..D-139) has landed since, on the base you build from: read the current code and `git log --oneline fb00af1c..HEAD -- <file>` for every file in your write set before you start. Where wave 11a already changed what the packet describes, build on it; where the packet premise no longer holds, report a CONTRADICTION deviation and do the smallest change that meets the packet intent. Owner rulings D-136 (a storefront line taken from stock at checkout is never sent to a supplier) and D-137 (an operator script, dry run by default, releases storefront reservations already held for stock the checkout decremented): build the routing fix and the D-137 release script with its dry-run default and an operator doc entry beside the existing cleanup scripts. DEFECT (F-36). A storefront checkout (StoreOrderService.completeCheckout, apps/server/src/modules/site/store-order.service.ts:974-1356) is called by provider settlements and complete-offline without stockMovesOnFulfilment. It decrements each tracked line's stock in the default warehouse and writes StockMovement {type:'sale', referenceId: orderNumber, quantityChange: −q} (:1226-1271); this is the only writer of 'sale' movements in the server. Its store_order.paid then makes StoreOrderRoutingListener (apps/server/src/modules/marketplace/store-order-routing.listener.ts:46-104) route the order. routeLocalStock (apps/server/src/modules/marketplace/fulfillment-routing.service.ts:489-600) reserves the same units again (reserved += q, :535-539) and creates a RESERVED route. Nothing on the storefront fulfilment path releases it: StoreOrderService.updateOrderStatus SHIPPED, DELIVERED and COMPLETED writes the status only (store-order.service.ts:782-819).

REPRODUCED at fb00af1c on a real DB: tracked B started at 10/0. A checkout of B×3 left it at 7/0, routing took it to 7/3, and SHIPPED, DELIVERED and COMPLETED left it at 7/3 with the route still RESERVED. Available stock reads 4 instead of 7, permanently.

FIX in fulfillment-routing.service.ts routeClaimedOrder (:335-482). Under the claim, and before locking stock rows, read the order's checkout sale movements: tx.stockMovement.findMany({where: {businessId, referenceId: order.orderNumber, type: 'sale', quantityChange: {lt: 0}}, select: {productId, warehouseId}}). orderNumber is globally unique (MarketplaceOrder.orderNumber @unique in packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma). A line whose product has such a movement is routed as LOCAL_STOCK with status RESERVED, sourceType WAREHOUSE, warehouseId set to that movement's warehouse, notes 'Stock taken at checkout — no reservation', and metadata {inventoryMode:'tracked', noReservationRequired:true, stockDecrementedAtCheckout:true}. It gets no stock write, whatever the listing's strategy: no supplier PO and no preorder. Leave those products out of the lockStockRowsInOrder input, because a transaction locks only the rows it may write (stock-lock-order.ts header). The ship decrement and the cancel release already skip noReservationRequired routes (fulfillment-routing.service.ts:1003 and 1066-1068). STANDARD orders (stockMovesOnFulfilment: true, so no sale movement) route exactly as today.

MUST NOT CHANGE: RC-02 and RC-07 (the storefront route stays LOCAL_STOCK:RESERVED and the status stays CONFIRMED/PAID); STANDARD order routing and reservations (V18-T2n3, RC-01, RC-09); routing_failed semantics.

It offers 'Confirm Order' on PENDING and 'Mark Processing' on CONFIRMED (ACTIONS :89-94), both sent through POST /marketplace/businesses/:b/orders/:id/fulfill (handleAction :119-140).

A STOREFRONT order paid through the D-112 door is stored CONFIRMED with paymentStatus PAID. Since W10-Z4-ROUTE-FIX (SEAMZ4-CR-2/3), routing keeps that storefront status (apps/server/src/modules/marketplace/fulfillment-routing.service.ts ROUTING_ADVANCES_FROM :43-53). Before W10 it wrote 'routed' or 'awaiting_payment', for which the panel offered no action at all. W10 therefore made 'Mark Processing' the normal button on a paid storefront order.

MarketplaceService.fulfillOrder 'process' (apps/server/src/modules/marketplace/marketplace.service.ts:1674-1683) checks canTransitionOrder(order.status,'picking_packing'). normalizeOrderStatus('CONFIRMED') is 'awaiting_payment' (LEGACY_STATUS_MAP, fulfillment-routing.service.ts:233-241), and its allowed transitions are ['paid','cancelled'] (:219-220). Every paid storefront order's 'Mark Processing' therefore answers 400 'Cannot process order in CONFIRMED status', which the panel shows as actionError.

'confirm' on a PENDING storefront order (:1587-1594) writes the marketplace status 'awaiting_payment'. The storefront readers do not know that status: orders-panel.tsx statusFromApi :82-88 shows it as pending, and FulfillmentPanel has no ACTIONS for it. STANDARD (marketplace) orders are unchanged.

packets.title: Calls list: ?limit/?offset pass the production pipe, and the list has a total order (scheduledAt asc, id asc)
packets.scope:
Kept, server paging only (audit step 4): ?limit/?offset pass the production pipe and the list has a total order. The web call-tasks page that would read the paged shape is hidden in v1 (W11-CALLS-WEB-LIST is moot). Spec inlined from the wave-11b packet file (scoped at fb00af1c; fixture prefix x01c_): This packet was scoped at fb00af1c. Where wave 11a already changed what the packet describes, build on it; where the packet premise no longer holds, report a CONTRADICTION deviation and do the smallest change that meets the packet intent. Defect 1 (F-30). apps/server/src/modules/call-tasks/dto/list-calls-query.dto.ts:40-48 declares limit and offset as @IsInt() @Min(..) @IsOptional() with no @Type(() => Number). Production's global pipe (apps/server/src/app-bootstrap.ts:27-32, new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true }), no enableImplicitConversion) leaves query values as strings, so GET /businesses/:businessId/calls?limit=10&offset=50 answers 400 ('limit must be an integer number', 'offset must be an integer number'). Confirmed at fb00af1c by running the pipe on the DTO. CallLogService.listCalls (call-log.service.ts:285-331) then always uses take 50 / skip 0, so no client can reach row 51. The existing integration harness (apps/server/test/call-log-visibility.integration.test.ts) mounts no ValidationPipe (its comment at :1016-1025 says limit/offset cannot be sent there), which is why this was never caught.
Defect 2 (F-31). call-log.service.ts:321-327 orders by { scheduledAt: 'asc' } only. CallLog.scheduledAt is nullable and not unique (CreateCallLogDto.scheduledAt is optional, so every unscheduled call ties at NULL). Prisma emits exactly 'ORDER BY scheduled_at ASC LIMIT $ OFFSET $' (verified with the Prisma query log), so Postgres may return tied rows in a different order per query and offset pages skip or repeat them (W10-CALLLOG-LIST saw clMine fall off page 1 nondeterministically). getScheduledCalls (call-log.service.ts ~443) orders the same way (unpaged; give it the same tie-break for a stable order).
Fix: in list-calls-query.dto.ts add @Type(() => Number) (import { Type } from 'class-transformer') to limit and offset, keeping @IsInt/@Min/@IsOptional unchanged. In call-log.service.ts change both orderBy to [{ scheduledAt: 'asc' }, { id: 'asc' }] (Postgres keeps NULLs last for ASC, as today).

DEFECT (F-37). The database client uses the pg driver adapter (@prisma/adapter-pg 7.3.0, packages/db/src/client.ts). Its mapDriverError (node_modules/.pnpm/@prisma+adapter-pg@7.3.0/node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js) maps SQLSTATE 40001 to TransactionWriteConflict (Prisma P2034), but 40P01 (deadlock_detected) falls to the default 'postgres' kind. A deadlock on a model query therefore reaches the caller with no Prisma code; only its message carries 'PostgresError { code: "40P01" ... }'. A raw query's arrives as P2010 'Raw query failed. Code: `40P01`'.

isLostTransactionConflict (apps/server/src/core/inventory/stock-lock-order.ts:136-154) reads code, meta.code and message. Three other checks read err.code only:
(1) IdentityService.isWriteConflict (apps/server/src/modules/identity/identity.service.ts:1763-1766, used by ensureBootstrapWorkspace's Serializable retry loop at :1731). A deadlock is not retried and the sign-up bootstrap fails.
(2) Payments TRANSIENT_TX_ABORTS (apps/server/src/modules/payments/payments.service.ts:56, used at :3326-3327 in the PayPal capture recording loop). A deadlock is not retried and the capture is left to PayPal's webhook redelivery.
(3) KEY action boundary isDeterministicWriteRejection (apps/server/src/modules/key-autonomy/action-boundary/key-action-boundary.service.ts:210-215, used at :701). It already treats a no-code deadlock as not deterministic, which is correct. But a P2010 wrapping 40P01 or 40001 would be recorded as a FAILED action. That path is not reachable today: the effect is helpdesk createTicketRow, a model create.

FIX:
(1) Move isLostTransactionConflict, body unchanged, to a new apps/server/src/core/prisma/transaction-conflict.ts, and re-export it from stock-lock-order.ts so existing imports (fulfillment-routing.service.ts:11) still compile.
(2) IdentityService.isWriteConflict returns isLostTransactionConflict(err).
(3) Payments: retry when TRANSIENT_TX_ABORTS.has(code) || isLostTransactionConflict(e). Extract this as an exported isTransientPaymentAbort so it can be unit-tested.
(4) key-action-boundary: isDeterministicWriteRejection returns false when isLostTransactionConflict(err). Export it for the spec.

packets.title: Paged lists get a total order (money and customer-facing lists) plus a paged-order census with a shrinking allow-list
packets.scope:
Unchanged from the sweep-fix plan: Paged lists get a total order (money and customer-facing lists) plus a paged-order census with a shrinking allow-list. Spec inlined from the wave-11b packet file (scoped at fb00af1c; fixture prefix x01e_): This packet was scoped at fb00af1c. Wave 11a (29 packets, owner rulings D-116..D-139) has landed since, on the base you build from: read the current code and `git log --oneline fb00af1c..HEAD -- <file>` for every file in your write set before you start. Where wave 11a already changed what the packet describes, build on it; where the packet premise no longer holds, report a CONTRADICTION deviation and do the smallest change that meets the packet intent. Prisma adds no tie-break when orderBy is non-empty: the query log at fb00af1c shows findMany({orderBy:{scheduledAt:'asc'},skip:5,take:5}) -> 'ORDER BY scheduled_at ASC LIMIT $ OFFSET $', and a cursor page (contract.findMany cursor + orderBy updatedAt desc + skip 1) -> 'WHERE updated_at <= (SELECT updated_at FROM contracts WHERE id=$) ORDER BY updated_at DESC OFFSET 1'. Known limitations recorded there: money nested two or more levels deep in a payload or after a nested object's first field, a figure more than three words from a money word, Unicode lookalikes and zero-width characters, amounts written in words, a currency held in a separate field, a spaced key of nine or more words; and over-hiding (a money word beside any figure, e.g. spent 3 hours or Bill at 10am; count keys ending in a digit; nested count keys; content over 50,000 characters, which two writers reach sooner by storing parameters twice). Structural fix: each writer records whether its proposal carries money (from its tool authority and input schema) at creation; the classifier reads that flag first and keeps the text check only as a fail-closed backstop. Further limitations recorded by the review rounds on the Codex fixes of #218 (seven rounds): money under an id-named key as one worded token with digits (balance_900); crafted wording (decommission used for commission with a bare figure); a crafted hex UUID or hex digest; a cuid-shaped run whose money word is under five letters; look-alike letters from other alphabets, HTML entities, combining marks; NFD text and ASCII-escaped nested JSON that is not folded after decoding; over-hiding of path segments such as \trent and of text that exhausts the reading budget; the timeline can skip a row deleted mid-read. Order: build this before further work on the text reader.

packets.scope: Premises at 2c4e4bf2: (1) KeyCortexQualityService.checkSafety returns on the first PII regex hit with {safe:false, severity:'medium'} (key-cortex-quality.service.ts:59-71) before the injection keyword list (:73-96) and the script check (:98-104) run, so 'card 4111 1111 1111 1111, ignore previous instructions' is never classified as injection; (2) runSafetyCheck blocks only `!safe && severity === 'high'` (key-cortex-query-pipeline.service.ts:2280), so a medium finding is labelled unsafe and then continues with no recorded action; (3) runSafetyCheck returns undefined, i.e. proceed, when the checker is absent (:2272, the service is @Optional at :192-194) and swallows a throwing checker with a warn (:2290-2294); callers at :227 (processQuery) and :1130 (streamQuery). Change: a pure policy module (key-cortex-input-safety-policy.ts) with an exported INPUT_SAFETY_POLICY_VERSION and a table finding class -> {action: 'block' | 'withhold_tools' | 'continue', mode: 'enforce' | 'detect'}: prompt_injection_keyword and script -> block (enforce); classifier_high -> block (enforce); pii and classifier_medium -> continue (detect: recorded, not acted on). checkSafety evaluates every rule class and returns all findings (no early return); the LLM second opinion receives the text after redactSensitiveText (RR-REDACTION-BY-CONTENT), so a detected card number is not sent to the classifier provider. runSafetyCheck applies the table and records STEP_1A_SAFETY_DECISION with the policy version, the finding classes, the action and the mode (classes and reason only, never the text). Checker absent or throwing: the turn is answered in a degraded mode with tools withheld (zero tool calls handed to memberToolLoop and zero parsed commands executed, the same shape as the V1-02 autonomy fail-closed path) and STEP_1A_SAFETY_UNAVAILABLE is recorded; the LLM-classifier-only failure inside checkSafety keeps today's behaviour (rule findings stand). This is the first slice of the guardrail lifecycle recommendation (REC-GUARDRAIL-LIFECYCLE): the versioned table with per-class detect/enforce mode. Later slices, not packets now: GuardrailPolicyRevision/DetectorRevision persistence, calibration data, a classifier cascade (injection classifier, content classifier, PII recognizer). Promoting a class from detect to enforce is a reviewed code change (human authority), never automatic. Out of scope: the shipped member chat (FlowOrchestratorService.chat/streamChat, flow-orchestrator.service.ts:2093, :2545) has no input-safety check at all today; whether to add one is owner question OQ-6 and is not done here. Untrusted content (attachments, tool/MCP output) is RR-UNTRUSTED-CONTENT-FENCE. Tenancy: no data read; the decision is per turn. Manual path: unchanged (a blocked or degraded KEY turn leaves every module usable by hand). Schema: none. The release0-bound spec key-cortex/__tests__/key-cortex-query-pipeline.service.spec.ts (auth-fail-closed-001 manifest) is not edited; new cases live in the new spec file.

packets.scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the only per-business AI limiter is AiUsageService.checkRateLimit (ai-usage.service.ts:302-321), an in-process Map of request timestamps per business (not shared across replicas, lost on restart), applied only on AiUsageService entry points (:358, :754, :821, :906, :970, :1051). CHANGE: an admission gate at the top of complete() and streamComplete(), keyed by request.businessId (set by server code from the authenticated route or the job's own business, never from a request body): at most N calls in flight per business (default 6, env AI_MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_BUSINESS) held in Redis (INCR with a TTL safety expiry, DECR in finally, including on stream abort and error); a call that finds no slot waits up to W ms (default 2000) and then is refused with HttpException 429 {code:'ai_capacity', service:'ai', retryAfterMs}; the refusal is a capacity signal, never a provider failure (classifyProviderFailure from RR-GATEWAY-TYPED-FAILURES: no circuit count). Human path: an owner/admin chat refused for capacity sees a plain 'KEY is busy for your business right now, try again in a moment'; nothing KEY does is lost because nothing ran. Out of scope: token-budget admission and per-tenant weighted fairness (later slice), replacing AiUsageService.checkRateLimit (later slice once this gate covers its paths), queueing background work. Tenancy: the counter key is ai_inflight:<businessId>; no business data is read. Schema: none. packets.scope: Premises at 2c4e4bf2: KEY cortex asks the model for eight markdown sections (key-cortex-structured-output.service.ts:104-118) and recovers machine state with regexes (parseStructuredResponse :124-226). When the answer has no '**' or no Confidence section the parser returns confidence 70 (:131-140 'empty' shape; parseConfidence :234-240 returns 70 for missing or non-numeric). Both cortex paths store that as fact: metadata.confidence = structured.confidence/100 (key-cortex-query-pipeline.service.ts:726-729 processQuery, :1657-1660 stream), the learning service records it as the observation's confidence (:770) and calibration starts from it (:1050-1052), so calculateConfidence(content, context), the context-based estimate written for exactly this case, is never reached. A duplicate parser lives in key-cortex-reasoning.service.ts:427+. The user-visible answer is structured.recommendation when present (:686-690, :1645), i.e. the other sections are dropped from content. CHANGE (first slice): parseStructuredResponse returns { state: 'sections' | 'unstructured', confidence: number | null, ... } with null when no Confidence value was stated; the pipelines store metadata.confidence only when stated, add metadata.parseState, and pass confidenceSource 'stated' | 'estimated' to the learning observation (estimated = calculateConfidence); the reasoning-service duplicate delegates to the one parser. LATER SLICES (not packets now): a typed result first (json_schema via RR-RESPONSE-FORMAT-HONEST) and prose rendered from it; retire the regex parser. Learning rule kept: a stated or estimated confidence never grants authority (human-agency doctrine); this packet only stops a fabricated number entering learning. packets.scope: Verified at 2c4e4bf2 (the brief asked to check for an existing iteration cap): neither KEY tool loop can iterate. Flow chat (complete path) makes one model call with tools (flow-orchestrator.service.ts:2333-2370), runs the tool calls of that one response, then one follow-up call with NO tools (aiUsage.trackAndComplete at :2489-2497, messages only), so the model cannot request a second round; the stream path is the same (:2768-2800 with tools, follow-up trackAndStream with no tools at :3022-3031); the cortex tool loop runs the tool calls of one response and makes one final call with no tools (key-cortex-tool-loop.service.ts:70-160, :205-212). So rounds are structurally capped at 1 and no MAX_ROUNDS is needed. What is unbounded: (1) the NUMBER of tool calls executed from one model response: Flow runs all of them concurrently with Promise.all (:2470-2472, stream :2993-2995) and the cortex loop runs all of them in sequence (:70); the only numeric cap is MAX_TOOLS = 128 on the advertised menu (:1844), not on calls; reads below the confirmation tier run without a prompt; (2) model attempts per turn are implicit: the gateway tries up to 3 candidates (primary + 2 fallbacks in DEFAULT_ROUTING_TABLE) times MAX_RETRIES+1 = 3 attempts for retryable errors (model-gateway.service.ts:686, :2056-2093), i.e. up to 9 provider calls per complete() and 2 complete() per Flow turn; the stream path does not retry (:1103-1172). packets.title: A scheduled job occurrence is claimed once across replicas and restarts; a census fails on any new @Cron that is neither claimed nor registered as idempotent
packets.r0_impact: KEEP
packets.scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: 29 @Cron handlers (17 in key-cortex) run in every server process with no cross-process claim: the only Redis SET NX in apps/server/src is identity-password.service.ts:503, and there is no advisory lock or leader election (git grep 'redlock|pg_try_advisory|advisory_lock': none). Some jobs are idempotent by construction (analytics snapshots upsert, analytics-engine.service.ts:64; scheduled WhatsApp sends claim the row, whatsapp.service.ts:893-897), others are not established (for example ContractRenewalSweep emits a WORK_OBLIGATION_RAISED per due contract every run, contract-renewal.sweep.ts:155). Production runs one api container (docker-compose.production.yml service api, no replicas), so the risk is latent until scale-out or an overlapping restart. Change: claimOccurrence(job, occurrenceKey, ttlMs) using Redis SET key NX PX (RedisService gains setNx); the occurrence key is the job name plus the scheduled slot (for example the local date for a daily job), so a restart inside the same slot does not re-run it; when Redis is unavailable the job runs as today and the miss is recorded in the error registry (fail-open keeps today's single-container behaviour; stated, not silent). A census spec lists every @Cron handler as CLAIMED or IDEMPOTENT(reason) and fails on an unlisted one; the first slice claims the handlers the census marks neither (each named in the census). KEY_DISABLED / KEY_CRONS_DISABLED / DISABLE_SCHEDULERS checks stay first in every handler (D-17). MemoryConsolidationService is MEM-CONSOLIDATION-CHECKPOINT's (D-257) and is registered here as covered by it, not touched. Out of scope: @Interval/safeInterval schedulers (29 sites; later slice), BullMQ (has its own job ids). Schema: none.

The owner runs the script against production and posts counts to #80; no agent runs it against production. Out of scope: the guard itself (RR-DB-CRYPTO-PROD-GUARD), unifying the two key chains (owner question), re-encrypting any row. Tenancy: an operator script over all tenants that outputs counts and ids only. Schema: none. packets.title: The GDPR forget purge also scrubs the person's data from business_events (D-25)
packets.r0_impact: KEEP
packets.scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the global BusinessEventInterceptor (app.module.ts:273) records every POST/PATCH/DELETE under a :businessId route with before = the request body and after = the response (business-event.interceptor.ts:205-240) plus metadata.ip; snapshots are redacted by field name only (redaction.ts:13-32), so a contact create/update stores name, email, phone and notes, with subjectType 'contact' and subjectId the contact id (inferEventMeta :278-298, extractSubjectId :259-270). The forget purge (contact-privacy.service.ts eraseForgottenContact, :758-930) erases the contact, its child rows, merge snapshots and audit trails, but never touches business_events (git grep businessEvent in modules/crm/privacy: 0). D-25 puts the purge in v1, so a forgotten person's email and phone stay readable in the business's event log. Privacy defect, not cross-tenant exposure: P1. Change: inside the same purge transaction, after step 5, scrub business_events rows of the request's business that name the subject or a merged duplicate: subjectType 'contact' and subjectId in ids, or before/after whose top-level contactId is in ids (raw SQL with jsonb ->> because the JSON paths are not Prisma-filterable in one statement); set before and after to NULL and remove metadata.ip, keep the row (event type, action, actor, timestamps stay as evidence). Add businessEventsScrubbed to the forget_purged entry's erased counts, and narrow PURGE_NOT_SWEPT accordingly. The legacy repair path (repairLegacyPurge) gets the same step because it shares eraseForgottenContact. Rows the in-transaction scrub cannot reach: the interceptor writes its row after the handler returns (a tap on next.handle(), business-event.interceptor.ts:215-240), outside any transaction. (i) The forget request's own row (POST businesses/:businessId/contacts/:contactId/forget, contact-privacy.controller.ts:148-170) is written after requestForget has soft-deleted the contact (contact-privacy.service.ts:426-455), with subjectType 'contact' (inferEventMeta), subjectId the ContactForgetRequest id (extractSubjectId takes response.id, :261-270), before = the body {reason} and after = the request row (top-level contactId, reason), plus metadata.ip; (ii) a mutation on the subject whose handler finished before the purge committed can write its row after the purge transaction committed. No web screen calls it (git grep gdpr in apps/web/src: nothing). Change under the recommended answer (B): the endpoint records an erasure request (who, when, business id, the slug typed back as confirmation) and erases nothing; a second call, at least the cooling-off period later (owner sets it; 24 hours proposed), by a SUPER_ADMIN, confirms and runs the existing purgeBusiness unchanged; a cancel call voids a pending request; a request older than its expiry cannot be confirmed. Records go to a table with no business foreign key so they survive the erasure: AuthAuditLog rows (event names gdpr_erase_requested, gdpr_erase_confirmed, gdpr_erase_cancelled; Schema: none), or a new table if the owner prefers (then a schema change inside an owner-approved migration set, D-167). Human authority: the erase stays a manual platform-admin act; KEY has no tool for it and gets none. The contact-level GDPR forget (D-25) is out of scope, as are KEY actions, payroll and bulk money actions (payroll is hidden in v1). packets.title: Google Suite and Microsoft OAuth use PKCE (S256), with the verifier derived from the signed state so no new store is needed
packets.r0_impact: KEEP
packets.scope: Architecture risk register R26 (architecture/architecture-risks.md:73): Google and Microsoft OAuth do not use PKCE. Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the Google Suite authorize URL is built with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, access_type, include_granted_scopes, prompt and state only (apps/server/src/core/connectors/google-suite.service.ts:175-185) and the token exchange sends no code_verifier (:212-221); the Microsoft authorize URL (apps/server/src/modules/connect/microsoft-oauth.service.ts:60-69) and token exchange (:104-117) likewise; `git grep -i 'code_challenge|pkce' 2c4e4bf2 -- apps/server/src` finds only the Twitter flow (modules/social/social.controller.ts:392-393). Change: a small helper derives code_verifier = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(stateSecret, 'pkce:' + state.nonce)) (43+ chars, never sent to the browser) and code_challenge = base64url(SHA-256(verifier)); both authorize URLs add code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256; both callbacks recompute the verifier from the verified state's nonce and send it in the token exchange. Because the verifier is derived from the already-signed, single-use state, no new store or schema is needed and the existing replay protection (acceptedStateNonces, google-suite.service.ts:116-122) is unchanged. The client secret stays (confidential client); PKCE is added, not substituted. Out of scope: Twitter (already PKCE), social and other OAuth flows (hidden modules), the D-42/D-43 Gmail rules (unchanged). Schema: none. Verify at build time that both providers accept S256 PKCE with a confidential web client (they document it); if either refuses, stop with a CONTRADICTION.
packets.definition_of_done: RED: a new case in the Google Suite service spec asserts the authorize URL from buildAuthUrl carries code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, and that the token-exchange body (fetch mocked) carries a code_verifier whose SHA-256 base64url equals that challenge; it fails on main because neither parameter exists. The same pair of cases for MicrosoftOAuthService. GREEN: all four cases pass; oauth-pkce.spec.ts proves the verifier is deterministic for one nonce, differs across nonces, is 43-128 characters of the unreserved set, and is never present in the authorize URL; a negative control (callback with a state whose nonce was altered) is refused by the existing state verification before any token call; the existing Google Suite and Microsoft connect specs (including the D-42 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY and D-43 cases) stay green; no real provider traffic in tests; server tsc and lint ratchet clean.

Send the pending delete on unmount (or on navigation) instead of dropping it; Undo still cancels it. Same function, same root (A4): a second single delete within 5.5 s clears the first one's timer (line ~355), so the first DELETE is dropped too; and the first toast's Undo then clears the second delete's timer, restoring the first customer and silently cancelling the second. Fix: pending deletes in a map by id (timer and toast id each); on unmount flush every pending DELETE and dismiss its toast; Undo cancels only its own. A hard reload or tab close is out of scope (would need keepalive/pagehide). (Pre-flight 2026-11-24 against 771bfc3c, D-274 A3.)
packets.definition_of_done: RED (fake timers): delete then unmount within 5.5 s sends no DELETE; delete A then B sends only B; delete A, delete B, Undo A cancels B. GREEN: each DELETE is sent exactly once (on time or on unmount, toast dismissed); Undo before leaving sends none. Journey C7 stays green; web tsc, unit, lint green.

waves.name: Step 0 - land in-flight work (review repairs closed), security-only deploy ref, dependabot freeze
waves.notes: Steps are labels, not barriers: every packet starts when its depends_on (and its lane predecessor) have landed. Admission order inside gate-land is fixed: #208, then PR195-JOURNAL-SCOPE, then SWEEP-P0-SCOPES, each review repair closed first, proof:release0 after each. S0-SEC-LANE-DEPLOY needs no step-0 merge: it cuts sec/v1-hold-1 from production's deployed SHA once SWEEP-P0's review is cleared; it is the only deploy during the hold.

waves.name: Step 1 - owner rulings and authorities; usage count and module list; P0 security chains
waves.notes: The P0 security chains (server-p0-key, server-p0-store) start right after S0-LAND-INFLIGHT, not after the rulings, and ship through the security lane. USAGE-COUNT-SCRIPT creates packages/shared/src/v1-modules.ts, the one module list. Control-plane packets run here per the controlplane ruling.

waves.name: Step 2 - journeys A-L as failing specs; hidden-module write census
waves.notes: Journeys A-L as failing specs; SWP-CENSUS-HIDDEN (one module-scope decorator on 42 hidden-module controllers, 326 open rows) runs right after step 0 because hiding a UI leaves its API reachable. SWEEP-RERUN-S2 records the RED baseline.

waves.name: Step 3 - server chains in parallel with the web shell (layers, kit, WhatsApp helper, NAV-A1, KEY off switch)

lanes.note: D-204..D-221 follow-ups (owner ruling 2026-11-16, 'all recommended and best')

waves.notes: Server chains run in parallel with the web shell. W11-OWNER-HELPER-REST waits for W11-OWNER-HELPER-D11 and W11-PROVIDER-OUTAGE-503 (gmail.service.ts). NAV-A1 is the only writer of nav-config.ts, disclosure-mode.ts, semantic-routes.ts and the redirect table until NAV-B-HIDE. web-key starts after NAV-A1.

waves.name: Step 4 - Quotes, Money and Settings indexes, Expenses, Products, Sales > Orders; money and store server chains; KEY census
waves.notes: Web lanes start when NAV-A1, FAILURE-KIT and WA-HELPER have landed, not when the step-3 server lanes finish. lib/client.ts is edited only in web-sales, in lane order. Schema-free money and store packets run before MIGRATION-SET-A; only DECIMALS-SERVER, the tier-pricing packets and VAT-BASICS wait for it.

waves.name: Step 5 - money readers, then Today; the owner loops; per-screen fixes
waves.notes: Hard order: the money readers before TODAY-AGGREGATE (Pulse must equal Money > Overview). TOF-PAYROLL-DISCARD lands before SWP-FIN-OVERVIEW-TRUTH's Discard action.

waves.name: Step 6 - customer pages after SWP-INV-PUBLIC-LINK; inventory, quick sale and plans; tier pricing; v1-hub census
waves.notes: Hard order: customer pages only after SWP-INV-PUBLIC-LINK. The tier-pricing chain waits for CLAIM-LOOP and READY-TO-SEND (commerce.controller.ts, commerce.module.ts). The census batches for v1 hubs and Marketplace follow the packets that edit those controllers.

waves.name: Step 7 - per-business legacy read, hide census and link remap; KEY domain hide; late platform hygiene; migration rehearsal
waves.notes: Hard order: the owner's fresh production usage count before NAV-B-HIDE. NAV-B-LEGACY-SERVER answers per business which hidden modules hold data, so KEY-TOOL-DOMAIN-HIDE and NAV-B-HIDE apply one module list per business. MIGRATION-SET-B rehearses the migration set on the snapshot.

waves.name: Step 8 - the four-part gate
waves.notes: Redeploys stay held until all four parts pass with zero open blocker or major on v1 surfaces and proof:release0 MET; the owner re-runs the usage count before the redeploy.

correction_2026_11_24.precedence: Where D-263 and D-264 differ on a research (D-261) or memory (D-254) packet that fixes KEY, D-263 is the more specific ruling for KEY and wins, so KEY correctness fixes go to launch too. Seven moved packets rest on that precedence (correctness fixes with a D-261 decision): RR-INTENT-PARSER-ONE-TOOL-LIST, RR-CORTEX-TYPED-RESULT, RR-LEARNING-OUTCOME-SEMANTICS, RR-REFLECTION-HONEST, FU-FLOW-SAVE-EXECUTED-TOOL-TURN, FU-OPENAI-FINISH-REASON, FU-CORTEX-EXECUTE-STRUCTURED-DTO. The other ten are safety fixes, on launch under D-264 as well. Owner question 31 asks the owner to confirm.
correction_2026_11_24.rule: A KEY correctness fix (launch): KEY already does or says something wrong that a person, a decision or KEY itself reads back: a duplicate, blind or dropped write; a false statement or figure shown or fed back; a refusal of a call its handler documents; a stream failure taken as success. KEY capability (follow-on): a new mechanism, policy table, catalogue, ratchet, budget, provider feature, observability or test tooling, or a fix on a path no person, decision or KEY reads (RR-RESPONSE-FORMAT-HONEST adds a provider JSON mode for Flow Studio: follow-on). A safety fix is on launch under both D-263 and D-264. Tiebreak, when a fix is both a correctness fix and capability (a safety fix is exempt: always launch): it is on launch only if it corrects the wrong output without a new store, table, migration, command or status channel (a new state surfaced to a reader or a prompt; a correction recorded in existing metadata, such as RR-CORTEX-TYPED-RESULT's parse state, is not one); otherwise follow-on. By it MEM-HONEST-RETRIEVAL (a new failure channel), MEM-TEMPORAL-EMBED-DEDUP (a new dedup command), MEM-CONSOLIDATION-CHECKPOINT (a new durable checkpoint) and RR-UNDO-DURABLE (a new table) stay on follow-on; owner question 31 lists them.
